12.3 Temperature Gradient A temperature gradient is a physical quantity that describes the direction and the rate with which temperature changes the most rapidly around a particular location. It is defined as the rate of change in temperature with displacement in a given direction. Symbolically, the temperature gradient is expressed as d dx . The SI unit of temperature gradient is Km-1. Here d is the small change in temperature over a small distance dx. The temperature gradient is a vector quantity.
Temperature Gradient for a Conducting Rod
Fig. 12.3 (a), Flow of heat through a lagged conducting rod]
[Fig. 12.3. (b) Flow of heat through an unlagged conducting rod]

Suppose a conducting rod of length l and well lagged from its curved surface as in figure12.3 (a). Let one end of the rod be in thermal contact with a hot reservoir maintained at temperature 1, and another end is in thermal contact with a cold reservoir maintained at temperature 2. At steady state conditions, a graph of temperature along the length versus corresponding distance is the straight line as in figure 12.3 (c). In this case the temperature gradient is uniform Δθ = θ1 − θ2 = constant . But for an unlagged conducting rod as in figure 12.3(b), the Δx l temperature gradient is not uniform, and the temperature falls exponentially as shown in fig 12.3 (d).
